lines.li: [us] What are the little vials on your coat?
[them] Storm rain, sealed, as Hesper Lyle sealed it after hail took her village's harvest.
[us] And what did that do?
[them] She wrote what came after on each cap, and in thirty years she read frost a week ahead.
[us] All of you can do that?
[them] Some of us, some of the time, and we are rarely wrong and never sure.
[them] Every storm over the plateau in three hundred years is written down in the tower.
[us] Why keep all of it?
[them] What the sky has done, it will do again, and the record is how we know when.
[us] Is a forecast ever wrong?
[them] Often, and we write that down too.
[us] What does a reader fear?
[them] The hail nobody saw coming, and a reader who is sure.
[us] Why a sure one?
[them] Because a sure reader stops looking, and the sky never does.
[us] Do you really sell the weather?
[them] We sell a day's warning, and a day is enough to bring the harvest in.
[us] And the rods on your roofs?
[them] They call the lightning down where it does no harm, and the glass writes the storm down.
[us] Why do you keep a seed in your pocket?
[them] For the next stump, as Elin Sedge kept one when the war cut down her valley for its fires.
[us] What did she do?
[them] She walked the stumps with a sack of acorns and planted one beside each, for years.
[us] And then?
[them] We buried her under the last one she set, and it still stands, and so do we.
[them] Every grove keeps a ledger of the trees round it, the felled and the planted.
[us] Including ours?
[them] Including yours, and we think better of a people who plant than of one who only cuts.
[us] And if we cut a great deal?
[them] Then someone comes with a sack of saplings, because we are here to collect.
[us] What do the Mossborn fear?
[them] Fire in the canopy, and a hillside cleared to the last stump.
[us] You seem so gentle about everything else.
[them] We are, until the forest burns, and then we are not.
[us] Do you never cut a tree at all?
[them] We take what falls, and we plant two for every one we must.
[us] Is that why your dead are buried under saplings?
[them] So the one who died becomes the grove, and in the end we are all the grove.
[us] Whose war was the Banner first raised for?
[them] A king nobody remembers, and when that war was lost Corra Mallin kept us together.
[us] What did she do?
[them] She sold every banner but the one burned grey, and hired us to the first town that paid.
[us] And the Roll?
[them] Those who stayed wrote down everyone lost under that banner, and we read it aloud still.
[them] Every name on the Roll is read aloud once a year, on the night of the last battle.
[us] Only your own?
[them] Anyone who fell holding a wall beside us, because nobody is left on the field.
[us] And the black sashes?
[them] The officers wear them for the dead, so nobody forgets who the Roll is for.
[us] What does a soldier of the Banner fear?
[them] A contract broken, and a field nobody came back from.
[us] Not dying?
[them] Dying is the work, but dying with your name left off the Roll is not.
[us] Would you fight for anyone at all?
[them] For anyone who pays, against anyone at the wall, never past the contract's last day.
[us] And if the pay stops?
[them] Then we walk, because no pay, no wall, and everyone knows it when they sign.
[us] What is the mark on your bracer?
[them] The guild's, from Oswin Kell, who rebuilt the Hardwater bridge three times after floods.
[us] Three times?
[them] He cut his mark into every stone of it, so the next flood would know whom to blame.
[us] Did it work?
[them] The fourth still stands, and those beside him swore to mark everything they made.
[them] Every journeyman spends a wander-year among another people before they are a master.
[us] Doing what?
[them] Working at their benches, learning what they know, and leaving a little guild work behind.
[us] And when they come home?
[them] They come back better, or they go out again.
[us] What does the guild fear?
[them] A cold kiln, and work that lies.
[us] How does work lie?
[them] It looks sound and is not, and bad work is a lie told in stone.
[us] Why does the guild pay so well for things other people make?
[them] Because a well-made thing is worth it from anyone, and we pay by the work, not the name.
[us] Even a stranger's?
[them] Especially a stranger's, because anyone can stack stone and few can do it well.
